title: Exact cost of the Fourier estimator
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For accuracy and confidence parameters $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2]$, every outcome in the support of the estimator's run-with-cost distribution has cost $(0,\,|\mathcal F|m,\,|\mathcal F|mn+|\mathcal F|m+|\mathcal F|m(n+1))$, where $m$ is the estimator's prescribed sample count per family member.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$\mathcal F$ is a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
$\varepsilon,\delta$ belong to the stated positive learning-parameter interval
The outcome belongs to the support of the run-with-cost distribution for the given target and estimator
